observations.content: Appeal from Judgment of High Court of Judicature at Patna in Appeal from Original Decree No. 4 of 1941, arising out of Judgment of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh in Title Suit No. 45 of 1939.

participants.name_or_role: Gangacharan Mukherjee and A. N. Sinha

observations.event: Case jurisdiction and procedural history defined.
observations.procedure_and_court: Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950; High Court of Judicature at Patna; Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh.

observations.content: The question is whether prior to the enactment of section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929, a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.
observations.event: Legal issue identified for consideration.
observations.procedure_and_court: High Court of Judicature at Patna.

observations.content: Raja Nilkanth Narain Singh mortgaged Gadi Sirampur to Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited on 1st August 1914. The Bank obtained a mortgage decree on 29th November 1921 and purchased a third share on 28th October 1922.
observations.event: Mortgage creation, decree, and execution sale details.
observations.procedure_and_court: Mortgage Suit; Court of Additional Subordinate Judge.

observations.content: During proceedings, Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages to Hiraman Ram on 5th November 1925. Hiraman Ram was Manager and Karta of the joint Hindu family.
observations.event: Permanent lease granted during pendency of mortgage proceedings.
observations.procedure_and_court: Mortgage Suit proceedings.

observations.content: An agreement was reached that if Wazir Narain Singh paid Rs. 1,10,631-4-0 by 16th August 1926, the sale would be set aside. He executed a mortgage to Court of Wards on 14th August 1926 to secure repayment and satisfy Bank dues.
observations.event: Sale set aside; new mortgage executed to satisfy original debt.
observations.procedure_and_court: Execution proceedings; Mortgage Suit.

observations.content: Plaintiff (via Court of Wards) filed suit on 4th February 1929 to enforce mortgage. Hiraman Ram and Dilo Ram were impleaded as co-defendants. Final decree for sale passed 18th September 1931; Plaintiff purchased on 6th April 1935.
observations.event: Enforcement suit filed; decree for sale passed; property purchased.
observations.procedure_and_court: Suit for enforcement of mortgage; Court of Additional Subordinate Judge.

observations.content: Dilo Ram died after mortgage decree. Hiraman Ram and Chohan Ram continued possession. Plaintiff filed suit on 16th November 1939 for khas possession against Hiraman Ram and Chohan Ram.
observations.event: Suit for khas possession filed.
observations.procedure_and_court: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh.

observations.content: Denied Plaintiff was subrogated to Bank's position. Contended decree not binding as he was not a party. Argued Patta not ended by auction sale.
observations.event: Written statement filed contesting Plaintiff's claims.
observations.procedure_and_court: Title Suit No. 45 of 1939.

observations.content: Denied being Manager and Karta of joint Hindu family. Contended partition occurred within a year of possession and properties allotted to Defendant 2.
observations.event: Separate written statement filed contesting family status and partition.
observations.procedure_and_court: Title Suit No. 45 of 1939.

observations.content: Held Plaintiff subrogated to Bank's position. Held Defendant 1 was Manager/Karta and Defendant 2 fully represented. Decree binding on defendants. Plaintiff entitled to possession and mesne profits.
observations.event: Trial judgment delivered.
observations.procedure_and_court: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh.

observations.speaker_label: High Court of Judicature at Patna
observations.content: Negatived constructive res judicata contention. Considered whether Wazir Narayan Singh had power to grant permanent lease. Concluded lease did not render Bank's security insufficient under Section 66 of Transfer of Property Act.

participants.name_or_role: High Court of Judicature at Patna

observations.event: High Court judgment dismissing Plaintiff's suit.
observations.procedure_and_court: High Court of Judicature at Patna.

observations.speaker_label: High Court of Judicature at Patna
observations.content: Held lease valid, not affected by Plaintiff's mortgage, decree, or execution sale. Dismissed Plaintiff's suit. Plaintiff obtained leave to appeal to Privy Council on 9th January 1946.

participants.name_or_role: High Court of Judicature at Patna

observations.event: Final High Court decision and Privy Council admission.
observations.procedure_and_court: High Court of Judicature at Patna.

observations.content: Both Courts below found Plaintiff subrogated to Bank's position and Defendant 2 sufficiently represented. Only surviving question: whether Wazir Narayan Singh had power to grant permanent lease to bind Plaintiff.
observations.event: Privy Council identifies sole legal question for consideration.
observations.procedure_and_court: Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950; Privy Council.
